[the rule's own record before the fold]
GR7 relates an alphabet-name to a coded character set, a collating sequence, or both. Table 6 and the a)-k) arms: a)/b) the class of the referenced set follows the ALPHANUMERIC / NATIONAL phrase; c) STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 are ISO/IEC 646 IRV in ISO/IEC 646 order; d) NATIVE is the native set of the clause's class; e) LOCALE is the named or current locale's sequence (kb/Work PB101); f)/g)/h) UCS-4 carries a set AND a sequence, UTF-8 and UTF-16 a set only, all three the D-N1 identity (implementor item 188, docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-188); k) the literal phrase, which kb/Work PB770 completed (k1a the 1-based ordinal into the native set of the clause's class, k1b a multi-character literal positioned leftmost-first, k2 the operand order as the ascending position order, k3 the unspecified tail above the highest specified position in native relative order, k5 THROUGH in either direction, k6 ALSO sharing one position with literal-1 as its representative). ⛔ i) IS NO LONGER VACUOUS (kb/Work PB793): code-name-1 is ASCII and EBCDIC (SR15's set), and GR7 i's three obligations are met per name by an ImplementorCodeNames row - ASCII is the ISO/IEC 646 IRV set with 128 ordinals, the identity correspondence and the native collating positions (i.e. GR7 c's STANDARD-1 answer under the spelling other vendors use); EBCDIC is IBM CCSID 37 with 256 ordinals, the collating position of a native character being its code unit in that page and the correspondence being the page itself, derived at bind time from Encoding.GetEncoding(37) and never transcribed. Every native character the page does not spell takes the position GR7 k3 gives an unspecified character, adopted here as this implementor's GR7 i specification - the SAME sparse CollatingTable the literal phrase builds, through the SAME CollatingTable.Build (which is also the one place GR8/GR9's extremes are computed). j) code-name-2 remains vacuous: SR15's national set is empty (DOC-A.1-184, DOC-A.1-185).

[folded GR-12.3.7.4-L2.1 = §12.3.7.4 7) d) 1.: CONFORMS]

Note: the stale in-code comment in AlphabetBind ('those three alphabet references are inert in this compiler today (no binder resolves them)') predates PB110's landing - documentation drift only. [folded GR-12.3.7.4-L2.3 = §12.3.7.4 7) k) 3.: CONFORMS]
Rule = GR7 k)3 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "Any characters of the native collating sequence that are not specified in the literal phrase shall assume a position" -> OK): unspecified characters follow the highest specified position, in unchanged native relative order. CODE: CollatingTable is sparse; an unspecified code unit c takes position NextFree + (c - |specified codes < c|), computed arithmetically at run time (LiteralPhraseCollation), over the full 65,536-unit set for both classes. MEASURED (probe/snp3/g9also.cob): ALPHABET AL IS "B" ALSO "A" ALSO "Z", "C" "Q" THRU "M" (7 positions) -> ORD("0") = 56 (= 7 + 48 + 1) and ORD("D") = 73 (= 7 + (68 - 3) + 1), "D" > "M". ca26_char_unicode_pcs derives that U+0100 keeps its native relative position above the specified block (k3). ALSO groups make NextFree smaller than the specified-character count, which the formula uses correctly (positions, not characters).

[folded GR-12.3.7.4-L2.4 = §12.3.7.4 7) k) 4.: PARTIAL until kb/Work PB1092 wrote DOC-A.1-186, now CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1092: Rule = GR7 k)4 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "If a character code set is being specified, the implementor defines the ordinal number within the character code set being specified" -> OK): an implementor obligation to DEFINE the ordinals of the unspecified characters, and Annex A.1 item 186 requires it documented ("The implementor shall document the scheme used for assigning the ordinal number" - 12.3.7 GR7k4). DEFINED in code: CodedCharacterSet.CharAt makes a literal-phrase set's ordinal = collating position + 1, so the unspecified characters follow in native relative order exactly as k3 places them (65,536 ordinals). MEASURED (probe/snp3/k4.cob, same AL as g9also): SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS S73 S74 S56 IS 73 74 56 IN AL -> 'D', 'E', '0' (agreeing with ORD under that sequence); CLASS CD IS 73 THRU 75 IN AL -> "DEF" in class, "DEG" not. NOT DOCUMENTED: docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no DOC-A.1-186 row although the CodedCharacterSet summary says 'documented in CONFORMANCE.md', and CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 27 states the opposite ('a literal-phrase alphabet's remapped ordinals (GR7 k4 leaves that correspondence to the implementor and this one does not define it)') - that sentence is about the on-medium CODE-SET correspondence, a different obligation, but it misattributes it to k4. Definition half verified, documentation half absent -> PARTIAL. The documentation debt is owned by open note A11 (Annex A.1 register); the k4 misattribution in row 27 is noted for that note.

[folded GR-12.3.7.4-L2.5 = §12.3.7.4 7) k) 5.: CONFORMS]
Rule = GR7 k)5 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "may specify characters of the native character set in either ascending or descending sequence" -> OK): THROUGH assigns the native run literal-1..literal-2 successive ascending positions, either direction. CODE: AlphabetLiteralPhrase's thru branch walks a -> b with step +/-1, Assign(advance: true) per character; SR14 b3/c3 one-character operands enforced first; a THROUGH+ALSO entry is refused (COBOL2242, PB790 landed). MEASURED (probe/snp3/g9also.cob): "Q" THRU "M" after two positions -> ORD("Q")=3, ORD("P")=4, ORD("M")=7 (descending native run, ascending positions). da1_alphabet_hex_thru derives the descending X"5A" THRU X"41" run (LOW-VALUE 'Z', 'A' above 'Z'); numeric-ordinal operands share the same path (LiteralPhraseOperand).

[folded GR-12.3.7.4-L2.6 = §12.3.7.4 7) k) 6.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1095 LANDED. Rule = GR7 k)6 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "If alphabet-name-1 is referenced in a SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS clause, only literal-1 is used to represent the character in the native character set" -> OK): ALSO operands share ONE ordinal position in the coded character set; literal-1 is the first character there; only a SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS reference uses literal-1 alone. COLLATING half CONFORMS (l1_char_national_also_positions). CODED-SET half now CONFORMS: CodedCharacterSet.CharAt answers ONE character (literal-1) for SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, and the new CodedCharacterSet.CharactersAt answers EVERY character at the ordinal for a reference that names a SET - a numeric CLASS ... IN literal (GR12 a). The reading is plural (the singular "a character" of GR12 a is read as the plural because the other reading makes k)6's exception sentence redundant): CLASS C1 IS 1 IN AL over ALPHABET AL IS "B" ALSO "A" ALSO "Z" is {B, A, Z}, pinned by 2002/pb1095_class_in_also_group (A, B and Z in the class, Q and the next ordinal's C not, SB IS 1 IN AL still B). An ordinal that names an ALSO group is no single character to begin or end a THROUGH run (GR12), so CLASS C IS 1 THRU 3 IN AL over it is refused (COBOL1671; negative pb1095-class-in-also-group-through).
